Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers up front, then details: yes, we support both card-on-file and monthly invoicing. Standard net terms are Net 30; Net 45/60 can be considered for enterprise customers after a simple credit review. For monthly invoicing we typically require a PO and either a small initial pre-commit or a credit/reference check — we can be flexible depending on expected monthly usage.

Details:
- Card on file: available immediately for self-serve customers, no minimum.
- Monthly invoicing: available for customers with either a monthly spend forecast above $10k or an agreed committed minimum for the first 3 months. Invoicing is done monthly with Net 30 by default.
- Net 45/60: possible but requires finance approval; usually needs either a longer-term committed spend or references.
- Discounts: volume-based discounts kick in at committed-spend tiers (e.g., 10% at $50k/mo committed, 18% at $150k/mo) — we can tailor for enterprise deals.
- Tax / W9 / vendor setup: we'll send a vendor onboarding packet and W9 if you're US-based.

I've attached our current rate card (redwood_rate_card_v2.xlsx) with published list rates and the standard discount tiers. Looping in Ben for the commercial side to discuss any tailored pricing.

Next steps I recommend: 1) confirm expected monthly consumption (tokens/queries) so we can propose a committed tier and discount, 2) if you prefer invoicing, have your procurement send a sample PO (we can issue an invoice referencing that PO), 3) finance fills the vendor setup form.

Happy to hop on a quick call with Ben/our finance contact if that helps.

Best,

Jordan — great to meet you over email. A few commercial clarifications and an initial offer:

1) Committed tiers & discounts (example):
   - No commit (card on file): list rates apply, standard monthly usage billing.
   - $30k/mo commit: 8% discount, Net 30 invoicing eligibility.
   - $75k/mo commit: 15% discount, flexible billing cadence, dedicated support.
   - $150k+/mo: 20%+ competitive enterprise pricing; negotiable SLAs.

2) Net terms: Net 30 is available out of the box for invoiced customers. Net 45/60 require procurement references and a short credit review with our finance team (Rishi copied). If you'd like Net 45 specifically, we can start the review now.

3) PO and vendor setup: We can accept a PO number on the invoice. For ACH, we'll provide wire instructions once the vendor onboarding form is complete and the legal team has the SOW in place.

4) Temporary solution: We can set up a short-term card-on-file while your procurement completes the vendor setup so there is no service disruption.

I've attached an initial SOW draft and a sample pricing doc for Acme (SOW_acme_initial_draft.pdf). If you can share expected monthly token counts or request volumes, I can draft a committed offer and update the rate card into a final PDF for signatures.

Thanks — happy to discuss on a call.

Jordan — thanks for the detailed follow-ups. Confirmations and next steps below: 

Billing cadence and due dates:
- By default invoices are issued on the 1st of the month for prior calendar month usage and are due Net 30 from the invoice date. If you require invoice-on-specific-day (e.g., the 15th), we can accommodate that in the agreement.
- Invoices will include any PO number you provide; please indicate the PO on the vendor onboarding form or in an email to finance@redwoodinference.com and we'll ensure it's on the invoice header.

Net 45 option:
- We can support Net 45 on a provisional basis pending a quick credit check. Your suggested approach (trade references + ACH on-file for first 60 days) is acceptable to our finance team in many cases — Rishi, can you confirm?

Late fees / interest:
- Standard policy: invoices past due may incur interest at 1.5% per month after a 15-day grace period. We can negotiate this for larger commitments.

Requested materials & next steps:
1) I'll upload a one-page commercial summary and a finalized rate card (PDF) after Ben provides the committed-tier numbers.
2) Please complete the vendor onboarding form here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_RateCardForm and include your AP contact and desired PO cadence.
3) Send the initial PO when ready; we will route invoices to the AP contact you provide.
4) If you want Net 45, authorize the trade reference check by replying to this thread and we'll kick off the finance review.

Attached is the final rate card PDF (rate_card_final_acme.pdf) prepared for Acme based on typical volumes. Ben — once Jordan shares expected monthly token counts, can you confirm the committed tier and I'll produce the one-page summary for their finance team?

Happy to set up a 20-minute call between AP and our finance manager to speed the vendor onboarding.
